topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This topic covers the introductory framing of the lecture, lecturer background, and key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer development and the balance of intrinsic versus environmental risks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental biology of cancer and evaluate the relative contributions of intrinsic cellular processes, genetics, and environmental exposures to cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the role of infectious agents in driving malignant transformation, focusing on pathogenic mechanisms and the case study of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific chemical and physical carcinogens induce DNA damage directly or through endogenous metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, chronic inflammation, and host tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic drivers of cancer development, focusing on the mechanisms of tumor promotion, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental vulnerability of host tissues.

topics.label: Methodologies for detecting and assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the genomic, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to identify carcinogen signatures and evaluate the carcinogenicity of exposures.
